list_companies.title: List companies
list_companies.description: Read every company in the account -- your own organisation and your clients. The cheapest call that proves the API key works, and the source of the company ids everything else needs.

output.description: `status` plus `companies`, each with id, name, project count and active flag.

get_company.title: Get a company
get_company.description: Read one company by id -- its name, project count and whether it is active.

id.description: The company's Beebole id, from list_companies.

create_company.title: Create a company
create_company.description: Create a company. `corporate: true` marks it as your own organisation rather than a customer. Send `xid` to give it your own external id, which you can then use instead of Beebole's id everywhere.

corporate.description: True for your own organisation; false (the default) for a customer.

xid.description: Your own external id for the company, usable in place of Beebole's id.

update_company.title: Update a company
update_company.description: Rename a company or change whether it is corporate. Addressed by its id.

corporate.description: Whether it is your own organisation.

activate_company.title: Activate a company
activate_company.description: Reactivate a deactivated company, putting it and its projects back in play for time logging.

deactivate_company.title: Deactivate a company
deactivate_company.description: Deactivate a company so no new time can be logged against it. Existing records stay and still appear in reports -- this is Beebole's archive, and the alternative to deleting anything.

list_company_members.title: List a company's exclusive members
list_company_members.description: Read the people or groups restricted to one company -- who may log time against it when it is not open to everyone.

attach_company_member.title: Restrict a company to a person or group
attach_company_member.description: Give one person or group exclusive access to a company. Once any member is attached, only attached members can log time against it.

person_id.description: The person to attach. Use this or `group_id`.

group_id.description: The group to attach. Use this or `person_id`.

detach_company_member.title: Remove a person or group's access to a company
detach_company_member.description: Undo attach_company_member. Detaching the last member makes the company open to everyone again.

person_id.description: The person to detach. Use this or `group_id`.

group_id.description: The group to detach. Use this or `person_id`.

list_company_custom_fields.title: List a company's custom field values
list_company_custom_fields.description: Read the custom fields attached to one company, with their current values -- industry, address, whatever your account defines.

output.description: `status` plus `customFields`, each with id, name and value.

set_company_custom_field.title: Set a custom field on a company
set_company_custom_field.description: Write a value into one of a company's custom fields. Field ids come from list_custom_fields.

custom_field_id.description: The custom field's id, from list_custom_fields.

list_projects.title: List a company's projects
list_projects.description: Read the projects belonging to one company, with their start dates, descriptions and subproject counts.

company_id.description: The company whose projects to list, from list_companies.

get_project.title: Get a project
get_project.description: Read one project -- name, description, start date, company and subproject count.

create_project.title: Create a project
create_project.description: Create a project under a company. `start_date` defaults to the first of the current month, which matters because time cannot be logged before a project starts.

company_id.description: The company the project belongs to.

start_date.description: Project start date as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the 1st of this month.

xid.description: Your own external id for the project.

update_project.title: Update a project
update_project.description: Change a project's name, description or start date.

activate_project.title: Activate a project
activate_project.description: Reactivate a deactivated project so time can be logged against it again.

deactivate_project.title: Deactivate a project
deactivate_project.description: Close a project to new time entries while keeping its history in reports. Beebole's way of archiving finished work.

list_project_members.title: List a project's members
list_project_members.description: Read who is assigned to one project -- the people allowed to log time against it once membership is restricted.

attach_project_member.title: Assign a person or group to a project
attach_project_member.description: Give a person or group access to a project. Attaching the first member restricts the project to attached members only.

person_id.description: The person to attach. Use this or `group_id`.

group_id.description: The group to attach. Use this or `person_id`.

detach_project_member.title: Remove a person or group from a project
detach_project_member.description: Take a person or group off a project, removing their access to log time on it.

person_id.description: The person to detach. Use this or `group_id`.

group_id.description: The group to detach. Use this or `person_id`.

list_project_managers.title: List a project's managers
list_project_managers.description: Read who manages a project -- the people who can approve its timesheets and see its costs.

attach_project_manager.title: Make someone a project manager
attach_project_manager.description: Give a person management rights on a project, which lets them approve time and see the project's billing and cost figures.

person_id.description: The person to make a manager.

detach_project_manager.title: Remove someone as project manager
detach_project_manager.description: Take management rights on a project away from a person.

person_id.description: The person to remove as manager.

list_subprojects.title: List a project's subprojects
list_subprojects.description: Read the subprojects under one project -- the second level of Beebole's tree.

get_subproject.title: Get a subproject
get_subproject.description: Read one subproject -- its name, parent project and active flag.

create_subproject.title: Create a subproject
create_subproject.description: Create a subproject under a project. Once a project has subprojects, time is logged against the subproject rather than the project itself.

xid.description: Your own external id for the subproject.

update_subproject.title: Update a subproject
update_subproject.description: Rename a subproject. Its parent project, members and logged time are untouched.

deactivate_subproject.title: Deactivate a subproject
deactivate_subproject.description: Close a subproject to new time entries while keeping its history.

activate_subproject.title: Activate a subproject
activate_subproject.description: Reactivate a deactivated subproject so time can be logged against it again.

list_tasks.title: List a company's tasks
list_tasks.description: Read the task types defined for a company -- "Meeting", "Development", "Admin". A task is usually required on a time entry, so this is the lookup before logging time.

company_id.description: The company whose tasks to list.

create_task.title: Create a task
create_task.description: Create a task type under a company, which time entries can then be logged against.

company_id.description: The company the task belongs to.

xid.description: Your own external id for the task.

update_task.title: Update a task
update_task.description: Rename a task type. Time already logged against it keeps pointing at the same task.

deactivate_task.title: Deactivate a task
deactivate_task.description: Retire a task type so it can no longer be chosen, without touching the time already logged against it.

activate_task.title: Activate a task
activate_task.description: Bring a retired task type back into use.

list_absence_types.title: List absence types
list_absence_types.description: Read a company's absence types -- holiday, sick leave, unpaid. Time off is logged as a time entry against an absence rather than a project.

company_id.description: The company whose absence types to list.

get_absence_type.title: Get an absence type
get_absence_type.description: Read one absence type by id -- its name, company and active flag.

create_absence_type.title: Create an absence type
create_absence_type.description: Create an absence type under a company, which time off can then be logged against.

company_id.description: The company the absence type belongs to.

xid.description: Your own external id for the absence type.

update_absence_type.title: Update an absence type
update_absence_type.description: Rename an absence type. Leave already booked against it is unaffected.

deactivate_absence_type.title: Deactivate an absence type
deactivate_absence_type.description: Retire an absence type so no new leave can be booked against it.

activate_absence_type.title: Activate an absence type
activate_absence_type.description: Bring a retired absence type back into use.

list_people.title: List a company's people
list_people.description: Read the people in one company, with their email, user group and team leader count. Person ids are what time-entry listing and approval take.

company_id.description: The company whose people to list.

get_person.title: Get a person
get_person.description: Read one person -- name, email, user group, company and team leaders.

create_person.title: Create a person
create_person.description: Add someone to a company. Supplying `email` creates a login for them, and `invite: true` emails them the invitation -- so this can reach a real person. `user_group` decides their rights: employee, contractor, pm (project manager), leader (team leader) or admin.

email.description: Their email address; a login is created for it.

invite.description: Email them an invitation. Only meaningful with `email`.

user_group.description: Their rights in Beebole. Defaults to employee.

xid.description: Your own external id for the person.

leaders.description: Team leaders to link them to, each identified by id, xid, email or name -- e.g. [{"email": "jane@example.com"}].

update_person.title: Update a person
update_person.description: Change a person's name, email, user group or team leaders. Setting `email` with `invite: true` re-sends their invitation.

email.description: New email address, which also becomes their username.

invite.description: Email them an invitation for the new address.

leaders.description: Replacement team leaders, each identified by id, xid, email or name.

list_person_leaders.title: List a person's team leaders
list_person_leaders.description: Read who leads one person -- the people who see and approve their timesheets.

deactivate_person.title: Deactivate a person
deactivate_person.description: Deactivate someone who has left. Their logged time stays in reports and they can no longer sign in -- the correct alternative to deleting them.

activate_person.title: Activate a person
activate_person.description: Reactivate a deactivated person, restoring their access.

list_person_custom_fields.title: List a person's custom field values
list_person_custom_fields.description: Read the custom fields on one person with their current values.

set_person_custom_field.title: Set a custom field on a person
set_person_custom_field.description: Write a value into one of a person's custom fields -- employee number, location, whatever your account defines.

custom_field_id.description: The custom field's id, from list_custom_fields.

list_groups.title: List the groups on an entity
list_groups.description: Read the groups assigned to one entity -- a company, project, subproject, task, person or absence type. Groups are Beebole's tag tree and drive reporting and permissions.

company_id.description: Read the groups on this company.

project_id.description: Read the groups on this project.

subproject_id.description: Read the groups on this subproject.

person_id.description: Read the groups on this person.

task_id.description: Read the groups on this task.

absence_id.description: Read the groups on this absence type.

output.description: `status` plus the `groups` assigned to that entity.

get_group_tree.title: Get the whole group tree
get_group_tree.description: Read every group as a nested tree -- the hierarchy of departments, teams, locations or whatever taxonomy the account uses.

get_group.title: Get a group
get_group.description: Read one group by id -- its name and parent.

create_group.title: Create a group
create_group.description: Create a group. Give `parent_id` to nest it under another group; without one it is created at the root of the tree.

parent_id.description: Parent group id. Omit to create the group at the root.

update_group.title: Update a group
update_group.description: Rename a group. Its position in the tree and its assignments are untouched.

delete_group.title: Delete a group
delete_group.description: Delete a group. Beebole refuses if the group is still assigned to anything unless `force` is true -- and forcing it silently drops those assignments, which changes what grouped reports return.

force.description: Delete even when the group is assigned to entities, dropping those assignments.

list_group_assignments.title: List what a group is assigned to
list_group_assignments.description: Read every entity carrying one group -- companies, projects, subprojects, tasks, people and absence types. Check this before deleting a group.

output.description: `status` plus the assigned entities, grouped by kind.

add_group_to_person.title: Assign a group to a person
add_group_to_person.description: Tag a person with a group, which is what Beebole's reporting and permission rules read.

remove_group_from_person.title: Unassign a group from a person
remove_group_from_person.description: Remove a group tag from a person, which drops them out of that group's reports and permissions.

add_group_to_project.title: Assign a group to a project
add_group_to_project.description: Tag a project with a group, so it appears under that group in reports.

remove_group_from_project.title: Unassign a group from a project
remove_group_from_project.description: Remove a group tag from a project, so it no longer appears under that group in reports.

list_custom_fields.title: List custom fields
list_custom_fields.description: Read every custom field defined on the account, with its id, name and which entity kind it applies to. The lookup before setting any custom field value.

get_time_entry_entities.title: Walk the tree to log time against
get_time_entry_entities.description: Ask what can be logged against on a date, one level at a time: pass nothing but the company to get its projects, pass a project to get its subprojects. The first step of creating a time entry, because the entity you finish on decides which id create_time_entry takes.

date.description: The date the entry is for, as YYYY-MM-DD -- availability depends on it.

company_id.description: Start from this company to get its projects.

project_id.description: Expand this project to get its subprojects.

output.description: The projects, subprojects or absences available at that level.

get_time_entry_tasks.title: List the tasks an entity allows
get_time_entry_tasks.description: Ask which tasks may be used with a company, project or subproject on a date. If any come back, `create_time_entry` requires one of them.

date.description: The date the entry is for, as YYYY-MM-DD.

company_id.description: The company to check. Use exactly one of the three entity arguments.

output.description: The tasks available for that entity and date.

list_time_entries.title: List time entries
list_time_entries.description: Read one person's time entries over a date range, with the entity, task, hours, comment and approval status of each.

person_id.description: Whose entries to read, from list_people.

from_date.description: Start of the range as YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: End of the range as YYYY-MM-DD.

get_time_entry.title: Get a time entry
get_time_entry.description: Read one time entry by id. Beebole wants the entry's `date` alongside the id, so pass both.

create_time_entry.title: Log time
create_time_entry.description: Create a time entry. Supply **exactly one** of `company_id`, `project_id`, `subproject_id` or `absence_id` -- whichever level get_time_entry_entities left you on -- plus `task_id` when get_time_entry_tasks returned any (absences never take a task). Logging against the wrong level is rejected rather than guessed at.

company_id.description: Log against a company directly, when it has no projects.

project_id.description: Log against a project, when it has no subprojects.

absence_id.description: Log time off against an absence type. Tasks do not apply.

task_id.description: The task, required when the entity has tasks defined.

person_id.description: Log on someone else's behalf. Defaults to the key's own person.

update_time_entry.title: Update a time entry
update_time_entry.description: Change a time entry's hours, comment, date or entity. Same one-entity rule as create_time_entry -- and an entry that has been approved or locked will be refused.

company_id.description: Move the entry to this company.

project_id.description: Move the entry to this project.

subproject_id.description: Move the entry to this subproject.

absence_id.description: Move the entry to this absence type.

delete_time_entry.title: Delete a time entry
delete_time_entry.description: Delete a time entry, given its id and date. The hours leave every report -- there is no undo.

submit_time_entries.title: Submit a timesheet for approval
submit_time_entries.description: Submit one person's entries over a date range for approval, which is what starts the approval workflow and notifies their approver.

from_date.description: Start of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: End of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

approve_time_entries.title: Approve a timesheet
approve_time_entries.description: Approve one person's entries over a date range. Approved time is what billing and payroll read, and it can no longer be edited by the employee.

from_date.description: Start of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: End of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

reject_time_entries.title: Reject a timesheet
reject_time_entries.description: Reject one person's entries over a date range. `memo` is the reason, emailed to the employee, so say what needs fixing.

from_date.description: Start of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: End of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

memo.description: Rejection reason, emailed to the employee.

lock_time_entries.title: Lock a timesheet period
lock_time_entries.description: Lock one person's entries over a date range so nobody can change them -- what you do once a month has been invoiced.

from_date.description: Start of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: End of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

unlock_time_entries.title: Unlock a timesheet period
unlock_time_entries.description: Unlock a locked date range so its entries can be edited again.

from_date.description: Start of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: End of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.

export_time_entries.title: Start a time export
export_time_entries.description: Queue an export of time records over a date range. `keys` names the columns and `status_filters` picks which records qualify -- "d" draft, "s" submitted, "a" approved, "r" rejected, "l" locked. Returns a job: poll get_export_job until it is done. Set `output_format` to "array" for structured rows instead of CSV.

from_date.description: Start of the export range as YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: End of the export range as YYYY-MM-DD.

keys.description: Columns to export, e.g. ["company","companyId","person","hours"]. Which keys are valid depends on `show`.

show.description: What kind of report to export. Defaults to "all".

status_filters.description: Record states to include -- "d" draft, "s" submitted, "a" approved, "r" rejected, "l" locked.

group_ids.description: Only records whose entities carry one of these group ids.

output_format.description: "array" returns rows as arrays; omit it for CSV.

company_id.description: Restrict the export to one company.

project_id.description: Restrict the export to one project.

person_id.description: Restrict the export to one person.

output.description: `status` plus the queued `job`, with its id and status.

get_export_job.title: Check an export job
get_export_job.description: Poll an export job. Keep calling (every 5 seconds or so) until `job.status` is "done" and `job.result` holds the data, or until the status is "error".

id.description: The job id returned by export_time_entries.

output_format.description: "array" to receive rows as arrays; omit for CSV.

output.description: `status` plus the `job`, whose `result` holds the export once done.
